title: Inertia-free finite stack covers are finite over the coarse scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field. Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over $k$ with finite diagonal and with a coarse moduli scheme $q:\mathcal X\to Q$. Use the meanings of stack, algebraic space, coarse moduli scheme and 2-fibre product spelled out in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Let $\nu:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ be a representable finite morphism of stacks; representable finite means that for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ the 2-fibre product $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is a scheme finite over $T$. Suppose that every object of $\mathcal Y$ over every algebraically closed field extension of $k$ has trivial automorphism group. Then $\mathcal Y$ is represented by an algebraic space and the composite $q\nu:\mathcal Y\to Q$ is finite. Consequently $\mathcal Y$ is represented by a $k$-scheme finite over $Q$. No condition of linear reductivity on the geometric stabilizers of $\mathcal X$ is required. Fields, schemes, finite type and finite morphisms use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori): separated universal-homeomorphism coarse morphism and its etale-local construction; Tag 045H in algebraic.tex (lemma-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms): trivial-inertia Deligne--Mumford stacks are algebraic spaces. Finite representable cover consequence and finite algebraic spaces over schemes, as used in Pikaart--de Jong Section 2.3.5 and Remark 2.3.7; agent-formulated consequence, not a verbatim Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-representable-finite-stack-properties] to $\nu$. Its scheme-test finiteness is exactly the representable finite hypothesis in the item, and its target is Deligne--Mumford. Thus $\mathcal Y$ is Deligne--Mumford over $k$, and $\nu$ is proper and locally quasi-finite as a stack morphism.

Apply [lem-sfb-dm-geometric-inertia-trivial] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ to the Deligne--Mumford stack $\mathcal Y$ from step 1. Every geometric point over this base is an algebraically closed field extension of $k$, so the hypothesis is exactly the assumed triviality of every geometric automorphism group. Obtain an equivalence $\mathcal Y\simeq E$ with an algebraic space $E/k$, as discrete stacks. This also removes automorphisms over nonreduced test schemes, not merely at geometric points. In Lean, first turn a fibre endomorphism into an isomorphism: the stack is fibred in groupoids, hence its vertical arrows are invertible. Apply the geometric automorphism hypothesis to this isomorphism and take its hom.

source.place: Tags 045H and 04SZ; geometric-stabilizer DM corollary recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dm-coarse-proper-locally-quasifinite] to $q:\mathcal X\to Q$. The hypotheses are precisely finite type over the field, Deligne--Mumford, finite diagonal, and the given coarse moduli scheme. Hence $q$ is proper and locally quasi-finite. No assertion that the coarse morphism is representable or finite is made here.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, combined with stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06U9, 06PU and 0CL5, as in the cited consequence.

proof.text: The scheme Q is a DM stack. Its discrete moduli category is fibred in groupoids by the explicit cartesian lifts in the category of elements. Mathlib subcanonicity of Scheme.etaleTopology.over S gives colimits of covering sieves, and their universal property glues the compatible maps to Q. Its diagonal tests are ordinary scheme pullbacks, and the identity atlas has etale surjective projections by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]; scheme objects are algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Compose the proper locally quasi-finite maps using [lem-sfb-stack-proper-locally-quasifinite-composition]. To transfer the result to E, construct an actual based quasi-inverse to the equivalence h_E → Y by transporting its ordinary quasi-inverse along the counit-induced base isomorphism. A based functor between discrete moduli categories uniquely comes from a presheaf map, by the tautological Yoneda colimit. The equivalence invariance and discrete-space compatibility in the composition node then give properness, the closed-immersion relative diagonal, and local quasi-finiteness of every etale scheme chart of E over Q.

Apply [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T=Q$ and source $E$. Step 4 supplies exactly its two assumptions: local quasi-finiteness for every etale scheme chart and testwise closedness of the relative diagonal. It gives a scheme $Z$ over $Q$ and an isomorphism $h_Z\simeq E$ over $Q$; in particular $Z$ is a $k$-scheme. The compatibility with equivalent stacks in [lem-sfb-stack-proper-locally-quasifinite-composition] identifies its structure morphism $g:Z\to Q$ as proper and locally quasi-finite in the ordinary scheme senses.

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme); stacks-morphisms.tex representable compatibility after definition-proper.

proof.text: Compose the representing presheaf isomorphism h_Z ≅ E with h_E → Y. The isomorphism over Q gives equality of its composite with qν and the discrete map h_g. Transfer properness and local quasi-finiteness to h_g with [lem-sfb-stack-proper-locally-quasifinite-composition], then use its discrete-scheme compatibility. The existing Scheme.Hom.isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff comparison for [pqf-def-quasifinite] supplies Mathlib local quasi-finiteness. Apply [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] to conclude g is finite. Finally, for every scheme test h_T → h_Q, use Yoneda to obtain T → Q, form T ×_Q Z, and use stability of finite scheme maps under base change. Its presheaf pullback yields an explicit equivalence with the discrete-stack 2-fibre product. The based equivalence h_Z → Y induces an equivalence on the right factor of this 2-fibre product, preserving the first projection strictly: full faithfulness follows from full faithfulness of h_Z → Y and essential surjectivity from the based quasi-inverse and its counit. Composing these two equivalences proves representable finiteness of qν, with exactly the specified projection. The 2-fibre lift and change-of-right-factor functors are the constructions in [def-sfb-moduli-chart-normalization]. No linear reductivity or surjectivity is used.

The Mathlib leaf for 02LS is the one already recorded on pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite.

The new nodes are true. (1) The coarse map is proper and locally quasi-finite. Finite diagonal gives finite inertia, so 0DUT applies, and the given q identifies with Keel–Mori's map because it is initial for maps to algebraic spaces. 0DUT makes q separated and quasi-compact, 06U9 makes it locally of finite type, and being a universal homeomorphism makes it universally closed with singleton fibres. q is quasi-DM because the diagonal of X over Q is unramified: it is the diagonal of X over k, which is unramified since X is DM, followed by a monomorphism. (2) A representable finite map to a DM stack has a DM source, by base-changing the atlas and factoring the diagonal; this works in the étale-stack convention of the definition node. Finite implies proper and locally quasi-finite. (3) Composition follows from 0CL7 and 06UD, and for algebraic spaces the stack notions agree with the ordinary ones via 04YS and étale-local quasi-finiteness. None of the new nodes restates the item or duplicates an existing node; I checked against abelian-level-coarse-moduli, unpointed-stable-coarse-projective, dm-finite-normalization-charts and unramified-diagonal-etale-atlas.
